after: ## Issues at global, national and local level
alt: Rings show mercury pollution locally (can a community eat fish from its bay), nationally (how tightly to regulate industry) and globally (mercury travels and builds up in fish worldwide). Below, the Minamata disease identified in Japan in 1956 led, decades later, to the global Minamata Convention on Mercury in 2013.
caption: A local problem may need action far beyond the place where it starts.

after: ## Issues at global, national and local level
alt: A four-step sequence: chemicals damage the ozone layer; the 1987 Montreal Protocol, ratified by every UN member state, phases them out; some replacement chemicals, HFCs, turn out to be strong greenhouse gases; the 2016 Kigali Amendment follows.
caption: Even a successful global agreement can have unintended consequences.

after: ## Perspectives: who thinks what, and why
alt: A spectrum from worried to supportive about a new protected area: local farmers, fishers and herders whose livelihoods depend on the area; a national government with mixed motives; tourism businesses; and conservation groups and international bodies backing the 2022 target of conserving 30% of land and sea by 2030.
caption: Explain why each group sits where it does, and remember individuals within a group can differ.

alt: A weak list of pollution causes contrasted with a chain: cheap production for export, factories cutting costs on wastewater treatment, untreated discharge where enforcement is weak, and falling fish stocks hitting fishing families downstream. A balance shows the trade-off of closing the factory: people downstream gain, workers lose jobs.
caption: Chains show analysis; trade-offs show that one consequence can help one group and hurt another.

alt: Nested circles: all Fenmoor residents contain a smaller group of the wetland charity’s newsletter readers, likely supporters already, which contains the 50 people who replied. The invented claim that 80% of residents want the wetland protected rests on this small, self-selected sample; a random household survey would be fairer.
caption: A self-selected sample shows what supporters think, not what everyone thinks.

after: ## Courses of action and their effects
alt: Five stacked bands of action from international agreements, national laws, market tools and local community action to individual choices. Below, a national ban on single-use bags is assessed: it tackles a visible waste source and is easy to enforce, but ignores other plastics and can be undermined by thicker bags used once.
caption: One action rarely solves an issue alone; judge it as part of a wider plan.
